analysis.investment_thesis: Elgi makes good compressors with a legitimate global ambition, but at P/E 42x (forward 35.7x) and FCF yield of barely 1.7% (INR 298 Cr FCF on INR 17,311 Cr market cap), I am being asked to pay a growth premium that the financials do not justify — OCF has been inconsistent (INR 35 Cr in FY20, INR 69 Cr in FY22), and the promoter holding of just 31.2% is a serious governance concern for me. I can find better quality at better prices elsewhere.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 10.7% and operating profit CAGR of 17.2% over 9 years demonstrate genuine competitive improvement in an engineering-intensive market
Global diversification across Australia, USA, and Europe reduces India-concentration risk and builds a multi-geography customer base
ROE of 20.1% and ROCE of 21.9% are above my minimum thresholds, suggesting the business does generate reasonable returns on employed capital
key_risks: P/E of 42x and EV/EBITDA of 32x leave virtually no margin of safety — any growth disappointment will result in severe derating; I have never paid 42x for any business in my life
OCF has been highly inconsistent: INR 35 Cr (FY20), INR 69 Cr (FY22), INR 166 Cr (FY23) — this volatility in a mature industrial business signals working capital management challenges
Debt/Equity has risen from 0.16x (FY20) to 0.26x today with borrowings at INR 528 Cr and CWIP jumping to INR 77 Cr — the company is investing heavily at peak valuations
red_flags: Promoter holding of 31.19% is deeply below my 55% threshold — this is the most critical red flag and tells me the founding family does not have adequate skin in the game

FY23 net profit of INR 371 Cr included INR 175 Cr of other income — stripping this out, core earnings were closer to INR 196 Cr, making the apparent 9-year profit CAGR of 23.9% significantly overstated
FCF yield of 1.7% (INR 298 Cr / INR 17,311 Cr market cap) is far below my 5% minimum — at this valuation, the market has priced in years of future earnings that may not materialise
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Elgi builds good products and the global compressor ambition is admirable — but I am a value investor, not a story investor. At 42x P/E and 32x EV/EBITDA, the market is asking me to pay for 10 years of growth upfront. My entire philosophy is built on not doing that. The operating margin of 12.2% is decent but not exceptional, and the inconsistency of cash flows (FY20 OCF of only INR 35 Cr on INR 1,829 Cr revenue) tells me this is a working-capital-intensive business where quality of earnings fluctuates.

The promoter holding at 31.2% is, for me, a dealbreaker. I built DMart and retained majority control because I was fully committed to the business long-term — I expect the same conviction from the promoters whose businesses I invest in. When I see a founder/promoter family holding less than a third of the company, I worry about who is truly guarding the interests of long-term shareholders. Combine this with an extreme valuation, inconsistent FCF, and rising debt, and I would rather wait on the sidelines for a significant correction before revisiting.
